# AI-Bench42

> Reproducible evaluation of local LLM coding agents, complete software delivery, independent verification, security gates, and human review effort. The current applied challenge is a multilingual email parser built from an empty starter.

AI-Bench42 asks a narrower question than generic leaderboard comparisons: can a coding agent integrate requirements into safe, working software and pass independent acceptance, not merely produce plausible code or pass its own tests?

## Current findings — read before citing

- **Only Kolibri-1 has reported local model trials** in this repository. Mistral, GLM, and Qwen are planned comparison candidates, not locally established winners.
- The latest independent Kolibri parser trial passed **21/21 supplied tests**, **10/10 self-authored tests**, and **24/27 supplemental probes**, yet **did not satisfy the complete project contract**. Missing integration and safety behavior remained.
- These counts do **not** establish 89% project completion, general coding reliability, German-language application quality, held-out real-mail accuracy, or human productivity savings.
- Published benchmark scores cited in the reports are external developer-reported numbers and not comparable to our local trial without matched conditions.
- The repository provides protocols, code, and selected evidence reports. It does not grant access to protected real correspondence, hidden evaluation data, or the private Melusense reference implementation.

## What the project is not

Not an independent cross-model leaderboard; not a verified claim that Kolibri can or cannot finish arbitrary projects; not a production-ready email parser; not a public dataset of customer correspondence.

## Use and citation

Cite the specific dated report and its methodology/evidence, and pin the Git commit. Confirm license and data rights before redistribution.

This `llms.txt` is a convenience map, not a guarantee of indexing, ranking, search visibility, or permission to access restricted material.
